entry.title: TCP and UDP and the relationship between them
entry.summary:
UDP

UDP is a bare-bones, lightweight transport protocol that offers only the most basic communication services. UDP is defined in [RFC 768], and it does about as little as a transport protocol can do. Apart from the multiplexing/demultiplexing function and some light error checking, it adds nothing to IP. In other words, if an application developer chooses UDP rather than TCP as the transport protocol, that application can be thought of as talking to IP directly, with no other wrapping around it.

entry.title: How to compute the UDP checksum
entry.summary:
How is the checksum constructed?

Constructing the checksum is fairly simple, but computing it is a bit of a pain: you add the 16-bit binary source data to be sent in pairs, keep the total to sixteen digits counting from right to left, and if there are extra digits you carry them round to the lowest bit and add again. Once all the data to be sent has been added up this way, you take its one's complement — that is, turn the 1s of those sixteen bits into 0s and the 0s into 1s.

entry.title: Blackhole routes
entry.summary:
A blackhole route is also a static route, but what makes it different from other routes is that a blackhole route's outgoing interface is NULL0. If a static route's outgoing interface is NULL0, we call that route a blackhole route.

Put simply, if the outgoing interface of a static route's network segment is specified as NULL0, then every data packet headed for that segment is dropped outright, with no forwarding.

entry.title: Quick Memory Joggers
entry.summary:
Brief

Here are a few simple JS memory points — just remember them and you're fine.

Quick notes

The difference between var and let

  1. The scope differs. var is function-scoped, let is block-scoped. For example, define a var variable inside a for loop and, as long as it lives under the same function as that for loop, you can reach the var-defined variable from outside the for; define a let variable inside a for loop and it cannot be reached from outside.
  2. let has to be declared before it is used; var can be used before it is declared, but until the declaration happens its value is undefined.
  3. let cannot be redefined, i.e. you can't use that keyword to define the same variable name twice; var can be redefined.

entry.title: How Vue3 and Vue2 differ on watch
entry.summary:
In VUE2, watch exists as an option. We can use the watch option to fire a function every time a reactive property changes.

export default {
  data() {
    return {
      question1: ''，
      question2: ''，
    }
  },
  watch: {
    // every time question1 changes, this function runs (shorthand)
    question1(newValue, oldValue) {
      console.log('question1 Changed!', newValue, oldValue);
    }，
    question2: {
        deep: true,// turn on deep watching
        immediate: true, // watch immediately when enabled
        handler(newValue, OldValue) {
            console.log('question2 Changed!', newValue, oldValue);
        }
    }
  },
}

  6. Agent Harness / Loop Engineering methodology (~12 days) — Andrej Karpathy, Dawn Song, and Andrew Ng repeatedly evangelize "how to keep an agent running for 40 minutes without crashing"; Karpathy's autoresearch, Hermes Agent v0.18-v0.19, and Gemini Spark's background loop are the practitioners.
